title: Feminine -ā nouns (लता, बालिका), singular

video.title: लता शब्द (आकारान्त स्त्रीलिङ्ग) अर्थ सहित
video.focus: Watch only the singular (एकवचन) column today, and notice that the 5th and 6th forms are the same: लतायाः.

recap: Day 27's quiz answers didn't come. Warm-up: (W1) Which case is हस्तेन? (W2) Say 'from the tree'. (W3) Say 'in the house'.
idea: Sanskrit nouns have three genders: masculine (पुंलिङ्ग), feminine (स्त्रीलिङ्ग) and neuter (नपुंसकलिङ्ग). So far you learned masculine -a nouns (रामः) and neuter -a nouns (फलम्).
Today: **feminine nouns ending in long ā** (आकारान्त स्त्रीलिङ्ग), like लता (creeper) and बालिका (girl). Unlike रामः, the 1st case has no visarga: just लता.
Note the 5th and 6th are the same form; the sentence tells you which is meant. The address form ends in -e: हे लते, हे बालिके. Some Hindi charts print हे लता; the correct Sanskrit is हे लते.
A pronoun must match its noun's gender: सः बालकः but **सा बालिका**; एषः → **एषा**; कः → **का**.
Hindi comparison: in Hindi the verb changes for a girl (लड़की पढ़ती है vs लड़का पढ़ता है). In the Sanskrit present tense the verb does **not** change: सः पठति, सा पठति.
Sound reminder: म् before a consonant is usually written as anusvara: मालाम् + पश्यति → मालां पश्यति.

examples.meaning: The student goes with the (female) teacher. (3rd)
Ramā gives a fruit to the girl. (4th)
The girl studies in the school. (7th)

sayAloud.meaning: O girl, where are you going?
That student studies in the school.
I read a book at home. (about your day)

quiz.q: Which is the 7th case (in/on) singular of लता?
quiz.why: 7th singular of -ā feminine ends in -आयाम्: लतायाम्. लतया is 3rd, लतायै is 4th.

quiz.q: Choose the right pronoun: ___ बालिका लिखति।
quiz.why: बालिका is feminine, so the pronoun is सा. सः is masculine, तत् is neuter.

quiz.q: बालिकायाः can stand for which two cases?
quiz.why: For -ā feminine nouns, 5th (from) and 6th (of) singular are both -आयाः.

quiz.q: Fill in 'to the girl': रमा ___ फलं ददाति।
quiz.why: 4th case singular of -ā feminine ends in -आयै: बालिकायै.

quiz.q: How do you call out 'O girl!' in Sanskrit? (Type the noun form)
quiz.why: The address form of -ā feminine nouns ends in -e: हे बालिके.
